extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, and editors of observational epidemiology research (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing clear, transparent reports of observational epidemiologic studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) so readers, reviewers and editors can assess strengths, weaknesses and generalisability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1(a) Title — indicate study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the study's design with a commonly used term in the title or the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should be able to identify the design from title/abstract. An explicit, commonly used term helps correct indexing (example: '...: a case-control study'). Avoid ambiguous terms; name the design early so readers can judge methods and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1(b) Abstract — informative balanced summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide in the abstract an informative and balanced summary of what was done and what was found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts should state the research question, concise methods and results, and conclusions. Present key numerical results (participant numbers, estimates of associations, measures of variability/uncertainty such as CIs). Structured abstracts with headings (background, objective, design, setting, participants, measurements, results, limitations, conclusions) are recommended; avoid only reporting statistical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2 Background/rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the scientific background and rationale for the investigation being reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context: what is known, gaps addressed, recent pertinent studies and systematic reviews. Set the stage so readers can judge potential contribution to knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3 Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: State specific objectives, including any prespecified hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives should specify populations, exposures and outcomes and parameters to be estimated. Distinguish prespecified aims from post-hoc analyses; if subgroup/additional analyses were not original aims, state that.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4 Study design — present key elements early
rubrics_metrics.description: Present key elements of study design early in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether cohort, case-control, cross-sectional or a variant (e.g. case-crossover) and describe the group(s) studied, timing, and basic principles of the design. Avoid vague terms like 'prospective'/'retrospective' unless defined; describe exactly how and when data were collected. If the report is one of several from a study, state that and refer to earlier publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5 Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the setting, locations, and relevant dates, including periods of recruitment, exposure, follow-up, and data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give recruitment sites/sources (e.g., registry, clinic), countries/regions/institutions, and exact dates for recruitment, follow-up start/end, and data collection. Dates place the study in historical context and affect generalisability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6(a) Participants — cohort studies: eligibility, sources, selection, follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohort study: Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants. Describe methods of follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report inclusion/exclusion criteria and the source population, recruitment method, and follow-up procedures. Describe completeness of ascertainment and whether follow-up methods were similar across exposure groups; give details needed to judge selection biases and loss to follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6(a) Participants — case-control studies: eligibility, case ascertainment, control selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-control study: Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of case ascertainment and control selection. Give the rationale for the choice of cases and controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how cases and controls were identified and sampled, and justify control selection strategy. Explain representativeness of cases/controls and potential biases introduced by control selection (e.g., hospital controls vs population controls).

rubrics_metrics.name: 6(a) Participants — cross-sectional studies: eligibility and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-sectional study: Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how the sample was defined and selected, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and sampling frame so readers can assess representativeness and selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6(b) Matching — cohort matched studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohort study: For matched studies, give matching criteria and number of exposed and unexposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe matching protocol (variables matched on, matching ratio), rationale, and how matching was implemented. Explain whether and how matching was accounted for in analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6(b) Matching — case-control matched studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-control study: For matched studies, give matching criteria and the number of controls per case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give matching variables and matching ratio, rationale for choosing matching variables, and analysis considerations (matching must be taken into account analytically in case-control studies).

rubrics_metrics.name: 7 Variables — definitions and diagnostic criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define all outcomes, exposures, predictors, potential confounders, and effect modifiers. Give diagnostic criteria, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise definitions and how variables were measured/constructed. Distinguish primary vs secondary outcomes, prespecified variables vs exploratory measures. State clinical or diagnostic criteria used and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8 Data sources/measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: For each variable of interest, give sources of data and details of methods of assessment (measurement). Describe comparability of assessment methods if there is more than one group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain instruments, questionnaires, laboratory methods, timing of measurements, validation/reliability information, and whether assessors were blinded. If different measurement methods were used across groups, describe comparability and any steps taken to ensure consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9 Bias — efforts to address potential sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any efforts to address potential sources of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss steps to reduce selection bias, information bias, confounding (e.g., design choices, measurement standardization, blinding, analytic adjustments). Explain likely direction and magnitude where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10 Study size
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the study size was arrived at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State sample size calculations or rationale for convenience samples, including assumptions used (effect sizes, power, alpha). If analyses were opportunistic or based on available data, explain limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11 Quantitative variables — handling and groupings
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how quantitative variables were handled in analyses. If applicable, describe which groupings were chosen and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether continuous variables were analysed as continuous or categorized; justify cutpoints; describe transformations. If categorizing, give category boundaries and rationale (e.g., clinical thresholds).

rubrics_metrics.name: 12 Statistical methods — full description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe all statistical methods, including those used to control for confounding, examine subgroups and interactions, handle missing data, address sampling strategy, and perform sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify models used, methods for selecting covariates, model-checking procedures, methods for matched data or complex sampling, how missing data were handled (e.g., imputation), and any sensitivity or supplementary analyses. Provide enough detail to reproduce analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: 13(a–c) Participants (Results) — numbers, flow, non-participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Report numbers of individuals at each stage of study (e.g., eligible, included, followed up, analysed), give reasons for non-participation, and consider use of a flow diagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts at each step (screened, eligible, enrolled, followed, analysed), explain exclusions and dropouts with reasons, and include a flow chart when helpful to clarify participant flow and potential selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: 14(a–b) Descriptive data
rubrics_metrics.description: Give characteristics of study participants (demographic, clinical, social) and information on exposures and potential confounders; indicate number of participants with missing data for each variable; for cohort studies provide follow-up time (average and total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present baseline tables with key participant characteristics, exposure prevalence, and distributions of confounders. Report counts of missing data per variable so readers can assess completeness and potential bias; summarize person-time where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15 Outcome data
rubrics_metrics.description: Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide absolute event counts, incidence rates, and/or summary measures appropriate to the design (e.g., prevalence in cross-sectional studies; numbers of cases and exposure distributions in case-control studies).

rubrics_metrics.name: 16 Main results — estimates, precision, adjusted/confounders
rubrics_metrics.description: Give unadjusted and, if applicable, confounder-adjusted estimates and their precision (e.g., 95% confidence intervals). Make clear which confounders were adjusted for and why they were included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both crude and adjusted effect estimates, list variables included in adjustment and rationale (or selection method), provide CIs, and when categorizing continuous variables give category boundaries. Where relevant, consider translating relative measures into absolute risks for interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 17 Other analyses — subgroup, interaction, sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Report other analyses done — e.g., analyses of subgroups and interactions, and sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish prespecified from exploratory analyses. Provide methods and results for interaction tests, stratified analyses, and sensitivity checks that assess robustness of main findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 18 Key results — summary with reference to objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize key results with reference to study objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Discussion, restate main findings in light of prespecified aims, emphasizing the most important results without overstating certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: 19 Limitations — discuss potential biases and imprecision
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limitations of the study, taking into account sources of potential bias or imprecision. Discuss both direction and magnitude of any potential bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about selection bias, information bias, confounding, measurement error, missing data, and statistical imprecision. Discuss how limitations affect interpretation and whether they likely over- or under-estimate effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: 20 Interpretation — cautious overall interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a cautious overall interpretation of results, considering objectives, limitations, multiplicity of analyses, results from similar studies, and other relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place findings in context of existing evidence and theory, avoid overstated causal claims from observational data, and comment on alternative explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 21 Generalisability (external validity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the generalisability (external validity) of the study results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the study population, setting, time period, and other factors that affect whether results apply to other populations or contexts; explain limitations to extrapolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 22 Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the source of funding and the role of the funders for the present study and, if applicable, for the original study on which the report is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding sources and any potential conflicts or funder influence on design, analysis, interpretation, or publication decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-specific and stratified reporting (starred items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information separately for cases and controls in case-control studies, and for exposed and unexposed groups in cohort and cross-sectional studies where indicated (starred items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the checklist marks items with a star (e.g., item 8*), report the required information separately by group to allow assessment of comparability and differential measurement/ascertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow diagrams and tables — use to improve clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use flow diagrams and structured tables to present participant flow, key baseline characteristics, and main results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flow diagrams clarify numbers at each stage and reasons for exclusion; structured tables (baseline characteristics, outcome counts, adjusted estimates) make reporting transparent and facilitate appraisal.
